title: CSV loader splits on '","' but Kaggle CSVs are only partially quoted — 4/5 match files and ALL players dropped
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:120,165,204,243,338 use line.split('","'). First data rows split into: Brasileirao=4 (<9), Brazilian_Cup=2 (<6), Libertadores=4 (<7), BR-Football=1 (<10), fifa_data=1 (<15) — all hit the len() guard and continue. Only novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (split(',') at :281 -> 13 parts) loads. Runtime log (_judge/attempt-001.stdout.log): 'Loaded 6886 matches and 0 players'.
suggestion: Use the csv module (csv.reader/DictReader) instead of splitting on a literal delimiter; the files are partially quoted with embedded commas.

title: Competition filter exists but only one competition's data loads
evidence: find_matches_by_team/find_matches_between_teams filter on match['type'] (brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:433,493), but because of R2 only novo_campeonato (all typed 'Brasileirão') loads — Copa do Brasil and Libertadores rows are entirely dropped, so the filter spans only 1 of 3 competitions at runtime.
suggestion: Fix R2 so Brazilian_Cup_Matches.csv and Libertadores_Matches.csv load.

title: No tool to search players by name
evidence: AST of brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py: the only player tools are find_players_by_club (:627, club+nationality) and find_top_players (:668, nationality/club/min_overall). No function accepts a player-name argument; the only 'name' function is clean_team_name (:365). Moot at runtime anyway since players is empty (R2).
suggestion: Add a find_player_by_name(name) tool that substring-matches soccer_data.players['name'].

title: Player nationality/club filters implemented but return nothing (0 players loaded)
evidence: find_players_by_club (:627) and find_top_players (:668) filter by club/nationality/overall, but load_player_data splits fifa_data.csv on '","' (:338, 1 part < 15 guard) so soccer_data.players is empty; both tools always return 'No players found'.
suggestion: Fix the fifa_data.csv parser (R2) so player tools return data.

title: No season-standings calculation from match results
evidence: No function computes points/positions. 'points' never appears in brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py; no standings/table/ranking function in the AST. get_team_statistics (:548) gives per-team W/L/D only; calculate_statistics (:714) totals matches/goals; find_biggest_victories (:767) lists margins. Nothing aggregates a per-season points table.
suggestion: Add a tool that groups matches by season, computes 3*W+D points per team, and sorts into a standings table.

title: Head-to-head returns a match list, not a W/L/D head-to-head record
evidence: find_matches_between_teams (brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:405) returns the list of matches between two teams but does not aggregate wins/draws/losses per side; the spec example (TASK.md:175) expects 'Flamengo 12 wins, Fluminense 8 wins, 7 draws'.
suggestion: Aggregate the matched games into a {teamA_wins, teamB_wins, draws} tally.

title: Tests execute (test_coverage=0.34) but do not successfully exercise the query tools
evidence: Query functions are nested inside define_tools() (brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:401-825); only define_tools is module-level (AST). integration_test.py:19,39 do 'from brazilian_soccer_mcp_server import find_matches_between_teams/get_team_statistics' which raises ImportError (caught -> test returns False). test_brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py only tests import + data-loading (tolerating 0 players). No test calls a query tool successfully.
suggestion: Expose the tool functions at module scope (or import via the registered MCP server) and assert on query results.

title: MCP import handled with layered FastMCP/Server/mock fallbacks
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp_server.py:19-40 falls back to a MockServer so the module imports without the mcp package; tools registered via @mcp.tool() in define_tools (:404).
suggestion: None — noted as robustness beyond spec.
